chapter_theme: Romarishi Njanam, an invocation and thirteen verses attributed to Roma Rishi, is a breath manual in the voice of a guru to a son: the two channels are moon and sun, release is their becoming one in the sushumna; the breath is drawn in sixteen and held at twelve; the horse (breath) is stopped between the two petals; the counted pranayama kindles the six centres up to the brahmarandhra; the tongue sent to the palate yields nectar and the silence of nirvikalpa. Round this it sets a polemic: silence or Vedanta-talk without yoga gains nothing, forest penance kills by lust, the man who calls himself a renouncer dies ignorant, and the span of life is a count of breaths, so that fate is what one has thought.
structure_note: 2455 is the kaappu and 2456 the poet's name-verse; 2457 states the thesis (no siddhi without yoga, none while women are desired); 2458 to 2460 give the channels, the counts and the stopping of the horse; 2461 is an aside on unfit disciples; 2462 to 2465 give the counted pranayama, the six centres and the ascent to the palate; 2466 and 2467 attack talkers and ascetics without yoga and define the two kinds of release; 2468 closes with the breath-count of a life.

2455.reading: Protection is the guru's foot that is the root circle; protection is the first that is the seed of release; protection is the supreme Brahman that is the circle above; protection is the truth that stands beyond Vedanta.
2455.nuance: A four-line kaappu that maps its refuges onto the body: the guru's foot at the root circle (mooladhara) and Brahman as the upper circle (the crown). வேதாந்தம் கடந்து, beyond Vedanta, sets the tone for the attack on Vedantic talk in 2466 and 2467.

2456.reading: Staying in the circle of time, seeing the milk of the moon's nectar and feeding his hunger on it, removing deceit from the mind, trusting the feet of the great ones who play siddhi in the circle of the world: by that the one called Roman became Nayan.
2456.nuance: A name-verse: the sage's name is explained by his living on the moon's nectar (மதி அமுதப் பால்), the fluid tradition holds to drip from the head in yoga, and by trusting the siddhas' feet. The three வட்டம் (circles of time, world, and the guru's foot in 2455) are a deliberate chain; how உரோமன் became நாயன் is not explained.

2457.reading: Covering a few mirrors and sending by the bow ... not knowing the embryo he died; the fault of not seeking and looking at the sky is the fault, and all his learning turned to mere earth; if one leaves yoga saying that silence is the one thing, there is never any siddhi, nor alchemy either; if one comes having left desire for women, I will speak the path of great bliss and release.
2457.nuance: The first two lines are obscure (கண்ணாடி சிலமூடித் தனுப்பினாலே); they seem to describe someone who hid behind tricks and died without knowing the source. The clear claim is polemical: mouna taken as the whole practice, without yoga, yields neither siddhi nor alchemy (வாதம்). Leaving desire for women is the entry condition for the teaching.

2458.reading: I will speak: the left channel is the moonstone; the right channel is the sun from the first; when the light that stood lovingly in the middle departs and then becomes one without departing, that is release; for those who looked with love, this is moksha here; for those who do not see, what is there but a body of lust? As a test, draw the breath up in the left channel, hold it in the sushumna, and you will be entranced.
2458.nuance: The cipher is stated and then decoded within the verse: இடைகலை is the moon, பின்கலை the sun, and the middle light the sushumna where they unite. சோதனையாய், as a test, invites the hearer to try the kumbhaka and see; சொக்குவீரே (you will be stunned, or absorbed) is the promised result.

2459.reading: Having drawn in, exhale within that twelve; is not the standing fire let go the sun's life? One who knows these two places is a yogi; the supreme foot that is reached is sixteen; the foot of the wind that held is twelve; drawing gently in the sixteen, holding what strained in the twelve and blowing, the risen city of eight has subsided: see.
2459.nuance: Twelve and sixteen are the Siddhars' breath numbers: the out-breath that runs twelve finger-breadths from the nose, and the moon's sixteen kalas, or an in-breath of sixteen measures held at twelve. Tradition reads பன்னிரண்டு as the sun's breath and பதினாறு as the moon's, matching 2458. புரியட்டகம், the city of eight, is the subtle body of eight parts; its subsiding is the goal of the exercise. The numbers are the whole content and their exact referents are not certain.

2460.reading: See: the horse's leap at the level is gone; do not let the sound out into the expanse; set it straight between the two petals and meditate on Sadasiva who fills them; if it goes four finger-breadths within the roof, it has drawn itself in and held within the mark, sir; who is your equal, I will tell you; you may be called my dear son.
2460.nuance: குதிரை, the horse, is the breath in the Siddhar cipher, and its leaping stopped is the breath stilled. இரண்டிதழ், the two petals, is the brow centre (ajna) in the usual scheme, and கூரை, the roof, the skull; four finger-breadths above is the crown. The last two lines are the guru adopting the pupil who achieves this as son, which 2461 at once qualifies.

2461.reading: Calling one son is good if he is a good child; adding unfit disciples is a fault; if you tell him the way to live he will not look at it; he is an ox who talks to warm his wife's heart; he took birth only to toil, and of help to himself there is none at all; this fellow's talk grows slighter and slighter: why do we say any more to him?
2461.nuance: An aside in the manual on whom not to teach: the householder bound to his wife and to toil, who hears and does not act. The guru's exasperation (ஏதுக்குச் சொல்லுகிறோம் இனிமேல்) is itself the lesson that the teaching is for the fit.

2462.reading: Whether sitting or walking, raise the essences without letting them go through other talk; four or eight, all is one; in the good eight-limbed practice, the siddhi of practice; if you first do pranayama as the measure, by count the filling and the holding are four, the emptying one and three; without shortfall join the sarabhi and finish.
2462.nuance: The verse gives a counted pranayama, but the ratio is garbled: பூரகம் கும்பகம் நாலு, ரேசகம் ஒன்று மூன்று may be the standard 1:4:2 with a number lost. சரபீ (also 2463, சரபீசம்) is unexplained; it may be a seed-syllable or a name for the combined breath. The claim that four and eight are all one is probably that the fourfold and eightfold yogas reduce to breath.

2463.reading: After practising joining, if you achieve the sarabhi-seed without lack, it shows the brahmarandhra; otherwise, by the mark of the eye, see it in the middle of eye and nose; it kindles the six adharas too: in the root circle Ganapati, then the four-faced one, then Mayan, in the strong manipuraka the ... circle, and the fiery Rudra, and the fire.
2463.nuance: The list of deities by centre is the usual Tamil scheme: Ganapati at mooladhara, Brahma at svadhishthana, Vishnu at manipuraka, Rudra at anahata, with 2464 adding Maheswara and Sadasiva above. கையன் வட்டம் is obscure. The brahmarandhra (பிரம ரந்த்ரம்) is the crown-opening the whole practice aims at; the alternative, gazing between eye and nose, is the easier method.

2464.reading: The fire becomes the vishuddhi, the six-cornered circle; is not Sadasiva's circle the guru's seat? If you mark it and look in the house of the sixteen, from the middle it takes the coal and smoulders and smoulders; if the fire keeps rising, there is everything; if you let the breath out, the deed is evil; the path of the welling water is this way; for the wicked traitor is it not false?
2464.nuance: The ascent continues: throat (vishuddhi, given six corners here though usually sixteen petals), then Sadasiva's circle, which is called the guru's seat. பதினி may be பதினாறு, sixteen; கரி (coal) and கனல் (fire) picture the breath as a smouldering fire that must be kept rising, and letting the breath out is called an evil deed. புனல், the welling water, is the nectar of 2465. துரோகி, the traitor, is the one who tells the secret or betrays the guru, for whom the path is false.

2465.reading: What is sent goes to the uvula and the palate, sir; climbing there, meditation appears by the way of the nape; the four have grown strong and become nectar for you; it has become the life called silence, without distinctions; hold it in the twelve where it sounds, and blow; the sixteen-fold digit of the moon has waned away; the siddhi of yoga and the siddhi of knowledge have borne fruit; in due season set the channel and make it practice.
2465.nuance: The tongue or breath sent to உண்ணாக்கு, அண்ணாக்கு (uvula, palate) is the khechari practice, from which nectar is said to flow. மவுனம் is here redefined as நிருவிகற்பம், the state without distinctions, reached through breath and not instead of it, answering 2457. சோடசமாம் சந்த்ரகலை தேய்ந்து போச்சு, the sixteen-fold moon has waned, is ambiguous: the moon's nectar consumed by the yogi, or the moon-breath exhausted. The four that grew strong are unexplained.

2466.reading: Without cover, teaching their small minds a lesson, preaching as if the whole had come to them, saying 'where is release, where is the body, where is yoga' in empty talk, did they not die? Climbing forests and hills, bathing in rivers, eating fruit, tubers and dry leaves, heated by the fire of lust, crores upon crores died; those who gained release with form were few.
2466.nuance: Two failures are paired: the Vedantin who denies body, release and yoga in words (வீடேது உடலேது யோகமேது) and the forest ascetic who starves the body but not lust. Both die; the verse's measure is that few reach சொருபமுத்தி, release in a form, which 2467 defines.

2467.reading: If you ask what the sign of release with form is: the gross body is seen like a flame; the place of release without form is the knowledge of Brahman, the hearing that is called indirect; if yoga is left, it becomes like the old tale of the small ant that said it would shift the mountain; like a fly that has entered an empty pot, they are barbarians who do not know Vedanta.
2467.nuance: The verse distinguishes two releases: with form, whose mark is the body shining, and without form, which is Brahman-knowledge reached by hearing. அபராட்சம் should mean direct (aparoksha), but சிரவணம் (hearing) is the indirect means, so the word may be a slip for பராட்சம். The polemic turns the Vedantin's own word against him: one who abandons yoga is the one who does not know Vedanta.

2468.reading: Om: listen, pupil of ruined mind; in the world a man's years are a hundred; is it not twenty-one thousand six hundred breaths in a day? Because they went, going out with the breath, the days diminished and were gone; if they do not go out, there is no going; when a man thinks one thing, the god thinks it too; are not fates only what one has thought?
2468.nuance: The breath-count of 21,600 a day is the standard figure of the hatha texts (fifteen a minute), and the verse's arithmetic is the Siddhar theory of life: a life is a fixed number of breaths, so the breath held is life saved. The last two lines go further and make விதி (fate) the product of one's own thought, with the god only concurring.

links.note: 2457 says that leaving yoga for silence gives no siddhi; 2465 restores silence as the life without distinctions that arrives once the breath is sent to the palate and held at twelve. Silence is the fruit of the practice, not a substitute for it.

Sivavakkiyar describes alchemy (வாதம்) as it is practised, a confidence trick with the fee taken and the alchemist fled; Romarishi holds that alchemy is real but unreachable without yoga and without leaving women. The one treats the claim, the other the trade.

Tirumular has moon and sun rising and falling through ida and pingala with life welling in the middle; Romarishi names the left channel moonstone and the right the sun and makes their union in the middle release itself.

Tirumular seizes the twelve female kalas and the sixteen male kalas and pours them into the fire for bliss; Romarishi draws in at sixteen, holds at twelve and blows, and the eightfold subtle body subsides. The same two numbers, with the sun and moon assigned to them.

Tirumular's unworthy disciple is the one who does not give up lust and does not fear birth and death; Romarishi's unfit disciple is the householder who hears the way to live and does not look at it. Both make fitness a condition of teaching.

Pattinathar says taking to the forest, eating wind and wearing rags gain nothing without inner love; Romarishi says those who climbed hills and ate dry leaves died in crores of the fire of lust. Both deny that bodily austerity by itself reaches the goal.

Both attack the preacher who holds forth: Agasthiyar's men who pore over books, call themselves gurus and shout that they are the Trimurti; Romarishi's talkers who deny body, release and yoga and die of their empty speech.

Tirumular's body made to shine without defect and turn gold by the Siva-water; Romarishi's sign of release with form, the gross body seen like a flame. Both take a shining body as the visible proof of attainment.

Tirumular reckons the span of life from the running of the breath, a hundred years if it runs five, eighty if four; Romarishi reckons it from the day's count of 21,600 breaths and says the days are lost as breaths go out. The same theory of life as a breath budget.

The Kural asks what is stronger than fate, which gets ahead of anything else one devises; Romarishi says fates are only what one has thought, with the god concurring. On the reading that 2468 makes fate the product of thought and not its master, the two claims are incompatible.

source_issues: 2457 lines 1-2 (கண்ணாடி சிலமூடித் தனுப்பினாலே) are obscure and possibly corrupt.
2462 and 2463 contain the unexplained word சரபீ / சரபீசம், and the pranayama ratio in 2462 (நாலு; ஒன்று மூன்று) appears to have lost a number.
2463 கையன் வட்டம் and 2464 பதினியிலே are unclear forms.
The invocation is numbered u1 in the unit id (siddhar:romarishi-njanam:u1) and the body 1 to 13; the chapter's own count is thirteen verses plus the kaappu.
